title: Cannoli: Crisp Fried Shells with Orange-Scented Ricotta and Chocolate Chips
summary: Crisp, bubbly fried shells piped with orange and lemon-scented ricotta, with mini chocolate chips and pistachio on the ends.
equipment: sieve lined with muslin or kitchen paper
piping bag with a wide plain or star nozzle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for the dough, the rest for sealing

ingredients.item: neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
lemon, finely grated zest and 1 tsp juice
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Drain the ricotta
steps.text: The night before, tip the ricotta into the lined sieve set over a bowl, cover and chill for at least 8 h. Removing the whey gives a thick filling that will not soak the shells.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Pulse the flour, sugar, salt and cinnamon in the processor, add the coconut oil and pulse to fine crumbs. Add 1 tbsp of the beaten egg with the grape juice and vinegar and pulse until it clumps, then knead on the worktop for 4 min until smooth and quite firm. Wrap and chill for 2 h; cover the rest of the egg and keep it cold. The acid in the juice and vinegar keeps the dough tender and helps the blisters form.

steps.title: Roll thin
steps.text: On a lightly floured surface roll the dough 3 mm thick and cut 8 rounds. Roll each round again into an oval about 2 mm thick; thin dough is what makes a light, shattering shell.

steps.title: Wrap the tubes
steps.text: Set a tube across the middle of an oval, fold one side over it, brush the edge with egg, then bring the other side over and press firmly to seal. Prepare 4 at a time.

steps.title: Fry the shells
steps.text: Heat 6 cm of oil in the heavy pot to 175 °C. Fry 4 shells on their tubes for about 2 min, turning often, until deep golden and blistered and the bubbling has calmed. Drain, leave 1 min, then hold with a cloth and slide the tubes out. Repeat with the rest once the tubes are cool enough to handle.

steps.title: Mix the filling
steps.text: Beat the drained ricotta with the icing sugar, honey, vanilla, both zests, lemon juice and salt until smooth, then fold in 30 g of the chocolate chips. Chill until needed.

steps.title: Pipe
steps.text: No more than an hour before serving, spoon the filling into the piping bag and fill each shell from both ends so the middle is full.

steps.title: Decorate
steps.text: Press the ends into the remaining chips and the pistachios, dust with icing sugar and serve.

tips: The most common mistake is filling the shells hours ahead; they go soft, so fill them close to serving.
Keep the oil at 175 °C: cooler oil makes greasy shells, hotter oil browns them before they crisp.
If the seal opens in the oil, press harder and use a little more egg next time.
Unfilled shells stay crisp in an airtight tin for 2 days.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store unfilled shells airtight at room temperature for up to 2 days and the filling in the fridge for up to 2 days. Filled cannoli are best eaten within an hour.
